newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bunds stay weak after Issing comments, but propped.
newsitem.headline: Bunds stay weak after Issing comments, but propped.

text.p: German Bunds stayed weak in late trade on Wednesday after sliding in response to remarks by Bundesbank board member Otmar Issing, who said there was no reason to expect further cuts in key German interest rates.
December Bund futures were quoted at 99.49 at 1507 GMT, down 31 basis points from Tuesday's close and near the session low of 99.45.
The contract had fallen about 25 basis points after Issing made what some analysts saw as an unusually categorical statement on monetary policy.
"Key rates are at a historic low here and nothing more is to be expected or necessary," Issing, the central bank's chief economist, said in an interview on German television.
Germany's economy was performing better than expected at the start of the year and there was reason to believe that the upswing would continue into next year, Issing told Germany's ZDF channel.
"That caught the market off guard, even if all facts were known beforehand," one bond dealer said.
But dealers said Bunds should remain propped by steady U.S. bond prices.

Issing's comments in the early afternoon breathed life into a stagnant market that had shown little reaction to news in the morning of an unexpectedly strong rise in September import prices which were up 0.7 percent month-on-month.
Traders also shrugged off the Bundesbank's downward revision in August industry output to unchanged from an originally reported 0.8 percent rise.
Dealers stressed that even if Issing had all but ruled out another cut in the three percent repo rate, there was no need to fear a rise in interest rates until well into 1997.
Bundesbank holds its next council meeting on Thursday. Most market participants did not expect a repo rate cut on Thursday even before Issing's comments.
